title: How would you design an autocomplete / type-ahead suggestion service (prefix lookups via a trie or an edge-ngram index, ranking suggestions by popularity/recency, debouncing client requests, caching hot prefixes, and bounding latency to a few ms)?
shortTitle: How would you design an autocomplete / type-ahead suggestion service
keyPoints: A trie or edge-ngram index makes prefix lookups a direct traversal, not a scan.
Pre-rank the top K completions at each prefix node so the request path is a trivial pinned-list read.
Debounce keystrokes on the client (150-300ms idle) to cut request volume dramatically.
Cache hot prefixes in Redis with a short TTL so common queries never reach the trie service.
Target single-digit millisecond latency: in-memory trie, pinned lists, tiny payloads.
Build the trie offline from query logs and catalogs; refresh scores in the background from usage events.
Fuzzy prefix matching for typos is layered on carefully, only when exact prefix returns too few results.

s1_definition.oneliner: Pre-rank the top completions under each prefix in a trie or edge-ngram index, debounce keystrokes, cache hot prefixes, and keep the whole lookup under a few milliseconds.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Trie / edge-ngram** – A prefix tree or pre-tokenized prefix index makes prefix lookups near-instant by direct traversal.
- **Pre-ranked lists** – Each node stores the top K completions already sorted by popularity and recency, so no sorting at query time.
- **Debounce** – The client waits 150-300ms after the last keystroke before sending, collapsing many characters into one request.
- **Cache** – Hot prefixes like "ho" and "lo" are cached in Redis so common queries skip the trie entirely.
- **Latency budget** – Suggestions must appear before the user types the next character: single-digit milliseconds.
s1_definition.analogy: When Rajesh types into National Bank of India's search box, as he types "ho" it should instantly suggest "home loan", "home insurance". Imagine a smart index where all known search phrases are filed by their first letters, and under "ho" there is already a short pinned list of the most popular phrases. The moment Rajesh types "ho", the clerk flips straight to that pre-written list. The box also waits a fraction of a second after he stops typing before asking (debounce).

sections.s6_takeaway:
Autocomplete has one brutal requirement: return ranked completions faster than the user types the next character, targeting single-digit milliseconds. At National Bank of India, a LIKE query returned results alphabetically and buried the most popular home loan. Pankaj replaced it with a trie where each prefix node stores the top K completions pre-ranked by popularity and recency, so the request path is a trivial pinned-list read with no sorting.

On the client side, debouncing collapses many keystrokes into one or two requests (a 200ms idle wait before sending), cutting volume by 80 percent. Hot prefixes like "ho" and "lo" are cached in Redis so common queries skip the trie entirely. The structure is built offline from query logs and the product catalog, and usage events refresh scores in the background without blocking reads.

For typos, fuzzy prefix matching using edit distance is layered on carefully, only when the exact prefix returns too few results, because fuzzy is more expensive. For a huge vocabulary, the trie is sharded by first letters across servers. The guiding principle is a read-heavy, precompute-everything mindset: move all expensive work (ranking, sorting, aggregation) to an offline path and make the request a trivial pinned-list read.

Remember one sentence: Store phrases in a trie with pre-ranked completions pinned at every prefix node, debounce keystrokes, cache hot prefixes, and move all ranking to the background so the request is a trivial list read in a few milliseconds.
